claims.text: Local chemical heterogeneity modulates stacking-fault-energy distributions and short-range or local chemical order.
Local chemical heterogeneity governs the activation of dislocation mechanisms in Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni and its quaternary and ternary subsets.
Differences in activated dislocation mechanisms produce differences in strain hardening and failure behavior.
Equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni can be prepared as a single-phase FCC microstructure.
Removing one or two constituents while retaining otherwise identical processing and microstructure isolates constituent-count or composition effects.
Reducing the number of constituents increases local compositional clustering.
Reducing the number of constituents broadens the distribution of stacking fault energies.
Spatially variable local chemical order and stacking fault energy alter dislocation slip, stacking-fault formation, and twinning.
Chemical and SFE inhomogeneity alters dislocation nucleation.
Changes in slip and twinning behavior modify strain hardening and ductility.
Quaternary and ternary subsets will have more heterogeneous local SFE distributions than equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni.
Quaternary and ternary subsets will exhibit more localized and less uniformly distributed dislocation activity than the quinary baseline.
Quaternary and ternary subsets may show more abrupt or lower strain-hardening rates than the quinary baseline.
Quaternary and ternary subsets may have lower ductility and less uniform deformation than the quinary baseline.
The equiatomic quinary baseline exhibits uniform deformation and consistent strain hardening because its local chemical environment is more homogeneous.
In FCC Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni, stacking fault energy controls whether deformation proceeds through perfect-dislocation slip, twinning, or transformation.
The proposed mechanism applies at room to moderate temperatures when dislocation slip and stacking-fault-mediated processes dominate plastic deformation.
Simpler quaternary or ternary compositions could be less costly than the quinary alloy.
APT or correlated high-resolution methods can quantitatively map local SRO and indirectly determine local SFE distributions.
